In addition, Disruptive Technologies' breadth of sensing also applies to SmartSense's existing markets in food and health while opening markets in building automation and occupancy.
"SmartSense and Disruptive Technologies together provide the building blocks for enterprises to operate more effectively by sensing physical operations efficiently at much greater scale," said Ron Konezny, CEO of Digi International. "Physical world intelligence is a foundational layer for enterprise AI, and this acquisition positions Digi to lead that category. We are excited to welcome the Disruptive Technologies team to the Digi family."

In addition, Disruptive Technologies' breadth of sensing also applies to SmartSense's existing markets in food and health while opening markets in building automation and occupancy.
"SmartSense and Disruptive Technologies together provide the building blocks for enterprises to operate more effectively by sensing physical operations efficiently at much greater scale," said Ron Konezny, CEO of Digi International. "Physical world intelligence is a foundational layer for enterprise AI, and this acquisition positions Digi to lead that category. We are excited to welcome the Disruptive Technologies team to the Digi family."

Should Investors Bet on Diodes After the ElevATE Acquisition?
Wed, September 30, 2026 at 7:45 AM PDT 3 min read
Diodes Incorporated DIOD has strengthened its growth profile with the acquisition of ElevATE Semiconductor, expanding its presence in the automated test equipment (ATE) market. The deal adds higher-margin analog and mixed-signal products to Diodes' portfolio and is likely to support its revenue and margin recovery.
ElevATE Deal Expands DIOD's Growth Opportunities

Visitors will also be able to explore examples from across the Diodes portfolio through application-focused displays for automotive, industrial, and data center systems. These will cover technologies including DC-DC conversion, MOSFET and bipolar transistor packaging, lighting, Hall-effect sensing, USB Type-C® power delivery, isolated gate driving, digital isolation, ReDrivers™, server interfaces, and PCI Express® clock generation.

Digi International Announces Intent to Acquire Disruptive Technologies to Advance SmartSense Physical-World Intelligence Platform and Enter Europe
Thu, October 1, 2026 at 4:30 AM PDT 4 min read
Acquisition combines Disruptive Technologies' best-in-class sensing with SmartSense AI and digital workflows to create a trusted data foundation for enterprise AI
HOPKINS, Minn., October 01, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Digi International (NASDAQ: DGII), a global leader in IoT connectivity products, solutions and services, today announced its intent to acquire Disruptive Technologies, a global leader in advanced sensing technology. Disruptive Technologies will join SmartSense by Digi, strengthening its critical monitoring platform and its ability to capture, interpret and act on real-world data at enterprise scale.
SmartSense built its platform around Sense, Understand and Act: capturing physical signals, applying AI and analytics to interpret them, and using generative AI and digital workflows to recommend the best next action to generate value. The acquisition of Disruptive Technologies significantly strengthens the Sense layer of the platform.
Disruptive Technologies brings leading, proprietary edge sensor technology to SmartSense enabling monitoring at scale with over 250,000 sensors deployed. Its sensors are smaller than a postage stamp, support a wider range of monitoring conditions, and operate for up to 15 years, much longer than other sensors in the marketplace. In addition, Disruptive Technologies' breadth of sensing also applies to SmartSense's existing markets in food and health while opening markets in building automation and occupancy.
"SmartSense and Disruptive Technologies together provide the building blocks for enterprises to operate more effectively by sensing physical operations efficiently at much greater scale," said Ron Konezny, CEO of Digi International. "Physical world intelligence is a foundational layer for enterprise AI, and this acquisition positions Digi to lead that category. We are excited to welcome the Disruptive Technologies team to the Digi family."
"This acquisition is about building an integrated physical-world intelligence platform where differentiated sensing provides trusted ground-truth data, AI turns that data into intelligence, and workflows translate intelligence into the best next action. Disruptive Technologies makes us better at every layer of that equation," said Guy Yehiav, President and SVP of SmartSense by Digi.
"Disruptive Technologies is driven by innovation to sense what matters," said Erik Fossum Faerevaag, CEO of Disruptive Technologies. "In SmartSense we found an organization that shares that same focus, combining market scale and reliable execution that will turn our sensing technology into measurable value for customers. Their strong customer satisfaction, execution, and scale give us an incredible platform to amplify what we've built."
The acquisition establishes SmartSense's first meaningful commercial presence in Europe, built on Disruptive Technologies' established European customer relationships and infrastructure across more than 25 countries worldwide. This will enable multinational customers to standardize on a consistent IoT monitoring platform across regions.
Digi executed a definitive agreement to acquire Disruptive Technologies for $130 million in cash, financed using Digi's existing revolving credit facility. In calendar 2025, Disruptive Technologies generated $15M in revenue and $4M in Annualized Recurring Revenue. Acquisition combines Disruptive Technologies' best-in-class sensing with SmartSense AI and digital workflows to create a trusted data foundation for enterprise AI
HOPKINS, Minn., October 01, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Digi International (NASDAQ: DGII), a global leader in IoT connectivity products, solutions and services, today announced its intent to acquire Disruptive Technologies, a global leader in advanced sensing technology. Disruptive Technologies will join SmartSense by Digi, strengthening its critical monitoring platform and its ability to capture, interpret and act on real-world data at enterprise scale.
SmartSense built its platform around Sense, Understand and Act: capturing physical signals, applying AI and analytics to interpret them, and using generative AI and digital workflows to recommend the best next action to generate value. The acquisition of Disruptive Technologies significantly strengthens the Sense layer of the platform.
Disruptive Technologies brings leading, proprietary edge sensor technology to SmartSense enabling monitoring at scale with over 250,000 sensors deployed. Its sensors are smaller than a postage stamp, support a wider range of monitoring conditions, and operate for up to 15 years, much longer than other sensors in the marketplace. In addition, Disruptive Technologies' breadth of sensing also applies to SmartSense's existing markets in food and health while opening markets in building automation and occupancy.
"SmartSense and Disruptive Technologies together provide the building blocks for enterprises to operate more effectively by sensing physical operations efficiently at much greater scale," said Ron Konezny, CEO of Digi International. "Physical world intelligence is a foundational layer for enterprise AI, and this acquisition positions Digi to lead that category. We are excited to welcome the Disruptive Technologies team to the Digi family."

Should Investors Bet on Diodes After the ElevATE Acquisition?
Wed, September 30, 2026 at 7:45 AM PDT 3 min read
Diodes Incorporated DIOD has strengthened its growth profile with the acquisition of ElevATE Semiconductor, expanding its presence in the automated test equipment (ATE) market. The deal adds higher-margin analog and mixed-signal products to Diodes' portfolio and is likely to support its revenue and margin recovery.
ElevATE Deal Expands DIOD's Growth Opportunities
Diodes completed the $250 million all-cash acquisition on Aug. 27. ElevATE develops highly integrated, low-power analog and mixed-signal ICs used in semiconductor test equipment.
Management expects ElevATE to contribute about $50 million in revenues during the first 12 months following the acquisition. Thereafter, it is projected to deliver a revenue compound annual growth rate of more than 20% over the next four years.
The buyout also gives Diodes greater exposure to semiconductor testing, where increasing chip complexity across AI, automotive and industrial applications is driving demand for more advanced test solutions.
Higher-Margin Mix Could Aid Profitability
One of the key attractions of the transaction is ElevATE's profitability profile. It generates gross margins significantly above Diodes' corporate average, and management expects the acquisition to be immediately accretive to revenues, gross margin and earnings per share. A greater contribution from higher-margin analog and mixed-signal products could therefore accelerate Diodes' margin recovery as factory utilization improves and demand conditions normalize.
The acquisition comes against a backdrop of improving operating momentum for Diodes. Second-quarter 2026 revenues increased 21.7% year over year to $445.5 million, while gross margin expanded 160 basis points to 33.1%.
Automotive revenues increased 37%, computing revenues rose 33%, supported by AI data-center demand, and industrial revenues advanced 24%. Non-GAAP earnings more than doubled to 70 cents per share.
These trends suggest that Diodes is benefiting from a broader recovery across several important end markets, providing a more supportive backdrop for integrating ElevATE.
Diodes has gained 88.4% over the past year compared with the industry's growth of 35.9%, lagging peers like FormFactor, Inc. FORM and ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. ASX. FORM has gained 251.9%, while ASX is up 307.1% over this period.
The ElevATE buyout strengthens Diodes' exposure to higher-growth and higher-margin semiconductor markets and the ATE market while complementing improving trends in automotive, industrial and AI-related computing demand. The deal could also help Diodes achieve its longer-term targets of $2 billion in annual revenues and more than $4 in non-GAAP EPS, providing a favorable setup for continued earnings expansion. Consequently, the stock appears to be a solid investment option in the volatile market.
DIOD currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

Diodes Incorporated (Diodes) (Nasdaq: DIOD) today announces that it will exhibit at electronica (November 10th-13th) for the first time. Visitors to Hall C6, Booth 211 will experience active demonstrations highlighting the company's expanding analog and power portfolio. Focusing on efficient 48V power conversion, motor control, and circuit protection, the Diodes booth will demonstrate solutions supporting automotive, data center, and industrial applications.
Under the theme "More than diodes," the company will demonstrate the breadth of technologies it provides for advanced electronic systems. Four demonstration platforms will highlight mains-to-48V conversion, 48V-to-lower-voltage conversion, motor control, and circuit protection. Together, these demonstrations will show how semiconductor selection influences power efficiency and system performance, highlighting the contribution of Diodes technologies throughout the signal and power chain. The booth will also feature numerous displays illustrating the breadth of the company's portfolio, from power conversion, protection, and sensing to isolation, interface, timing, and connectivity technologies.
The 48V power tree demonstration will illustrate power conversion from a 48V input to 12V and then to lower-voltage rails, including 5V and 3.3V. Visitors will observe current flow through different stages and see the impact of component selection on conversion efficiency. The demonstration reflects the increasing importance of 48V architectures in automotive and industrial applications, where efficient conversion and distribution of electrical power are key design considerations.
A separate motor control demonstration will show the role of Diodes' power and analog components around a third-party microprocessor and provide visibility of motor efficiency during operation. A circuit protection demonstration will compare different approaches to reverse battery protection, from a simple diode implementation through to a higher-efficiency approach based on an ideal diode controller, enabling visitors to explore the trade-offs between component cost and power efficiency.
Diodes will use its presence at electronica 2026 to unveil the latest in power-conversion technology addressing the requirements of data center and AI computing infrastructure. Visitors will also be able to explore examples from across the Diodes portfolio through application-focused displays for automotive, industrial, and data center systems. These will cover technologies including DC-DC conversion, MOSFET and bipolar transistor packaging, lighting, Hall-effect sensing, USB Type-C® power delivery, isolated gate driving, digital isolation, ReDrivers™, server interfaces, and PCI Express® clock generation.
Emily Yang, SVP Sales & Marketing, Diodes Incorporated, said: "As power architectures become more complex, customers need solutions that improve efficiency across the complete system, not simply at the component level. At electronica, we will demonstrate how Diodes' expanding analog and power portfolio helps engineers address conversion, control, and protection challenges across automotive, industrial, and data center applications."

Should Investors Bet on Diodes After the ElevATE Acquisition?
Wed, September 30, 2026 at 7:45 AM PDT 3 min read
Diodes Incorporated DIOD has strengthened its growth profile with the acquisition of ElevATE Semiconductor, expanding its presence in the automated test equipment (ATE) market. The deal adds higher-margin analog and mixed-signal products to Diodes' portfolio and is likely to support its revenue and margin recovery.
ElevATE Deal Expands DIOD's Growth Opportunities
Diodes completed the $250 million all-cash acquisition on Aug. 27. ElevATE develops highly integrated, low-power analog and mixed-signal ICs used in semiconductor test equipment.
Management expects ElevATE to contribute about $50 million in revenues during the first 12 months following the acquisition. Thereafter, it is projected to deliver a revenue compound annual growth rate of more than 20% over the next four years.
The buyout also gives Diodes greater exposure to semiconductor testing, where increasing chip complexity across AI, automotive and industrial applications is driving demand for more advanced test solutions.
Higher-Margin Mix Could Aid Profitability
One of the key attractions of the transaction is ElevATE's profitability profile. It generates gross margins significantly above Diodes' corporate average, and management expects the acquisition to be immediately accretive to revenues, gross margin and earnings per share. A greater contribution from higher-margin analog and mixed-signal products could therefore accelerate Diodes' margin recovery as factory utilization improves and demand conditions normalize.
The acquisition comes against a backdrop of improving operating momentum for Diodes. Second-quarter 2026 revenues increased 21.7% year over year to $445.5 million, while gross margin expanded 160 basis points to 33.1%.
Automotive revenues increased 37%, computing revenues rose 33%, supported by AI data-center demand, and industrial revenues advanced 24%. Non-GAAP earnings more than doubled to 70 cents per share.
These trends suggest that Diodes is benefiting from a broader recovery across several important end markets, providing a more supportive backdrop for integrating ElevATE.
Diodes has gained 88.4% over the past year compared with the industry's growth of 35.9%, lagging peers like FormFactor, Inc. FORM and ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. ASX. FORM has gained 251.9%, while ASX is up 307.1% over this period.
The ElevATE buyout strengthens Diodes' exposure to higher-growth and higher-margin semiconductor markets and the ATE market while complementing improving trends in automotive, industrial and AI-related computing demand. The deal could also help Diodes achieve its longer-term targets of $2 billion in annual revenues and more than $4 in non-GAAP EPS, providing a favorable setup for continued earnings expansion. Consequently, the stock appears to be a solid investment option in the volatile market.

Diodes Incorporated : Showcases Analog and Power Solutions for Efficient Automotive, Data Center, and Industrial Systems at electronica 2026
Diodes Incorporated (Diodes) (Nasdaq: DIOD) today announces that it will exhibit at electronica (November 10th-13th) for the first time. Visitors to Hall C6, Booth 211 will experience active demonstrations highlighting the company's expanding analog and power portfolio. Focusing on efficient 48V power conversion, motor control, and circuit protection, the Diodes booth will demonstrate solutions supporting automotive, data center, and industrial applications.
Under the theme "More than diodes," the company will demonstrate the breadth of technologies it provides for advanced electronic systems. Four demonstration platforms will highlight mains-to-48V conversion, 48V-to-lower-voltage conversion, motor control, and circuit protection. Together, these demonstrations will show how semiconductor selection influences power efficiency and system performance, highlighting the contribution of Diodes technologies throughout the signal and power chain. The booth will also feature numerous displays illustrating the breadth of the company's portfolio, from power conversion, protection, and sensing to isolation, interface, timing, and connectivity technologies.
The 48V power tree demonstration will illustrate power conversion from a 48V input to 12V and then to lower-voltage rails, including 5V and 3.3V. Visitors will observe current flow through different stages and see the impact of component selection on conversion efficiency. The demonstration reflects the increasing importance of 48V architectures in automotive and industrial applications, where efficient conversion and distribution of electrical power are key design considerations.
A separate motor control demonstration will show the role of Diodes' power and analog components around a third-party microprocessor and provide visibility of motor efficiency during operation. A circuit protection demonstration will compare different approaches to reverse battery protection, from a simple diode implementation through to a higher-efficiency approach based on an ideal diode controller, enabling visitors to explore the trade-offs between component cost and power efficiency.
Diodes will use its presence at electronica 2026 to unveil the latest in power-conversion technology addressing the requirements of data center and AI computing infrastructure. Visitors will also be able to explore examples from across the Diodes portfolio through application-focused displays for automotive, industrial, and data center systems. These will cover technologies including DC-DC conversion, MOSFET and bipolar transistor packaging, lighting, Hall-effect sensing, USB Type-C® power delivery, isolated gate driving, digital isolation, ReDrivers™, server interfaces, and PCI Express® clock generation.
Emily Yang, SVP Sales & Marketing, Diodes Incorporated, said: "As power architectures become more complex, customers need solutions that improve efficiency across the complete system, not simply at the component level. At electronica, we will demonstrate how Diodes' expanding analog and power portfolio helps engineers address conversion, control, and protection challenges across automotive, industrial, and data center applications."
To arrange a meeting with a Diodes representative during electronica 2026, please visit the following link to register your interest:https://www.diodes.com/about/news/events/electronica-2026
